messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool hotpath-prod reporting sustained queue growth and elevated 429s. 95% pool utilization, 6000 queued requests, 12% global 429 rate over the last 5m. Pager: @oncall-sre. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-exhaustion

oncall-sre: I'm on it. any customer impact flagged?

amanda-sales: getting messages from two enterprise customers about client-side 429 spikes, they see timeouts and retries. escalated to SEs.

raj: looking at autoscaler logs now — seeing repeated failures creating nodes: 
```
ERROR: Failed to allocate instance: QuotaExceeded: GPUs quota 0 -> requested 4
caused_by: projects/prod/quotas/gpus
```
This started ~3117769800, autoscaler kept retrying and hit backoff.

maria: if autoscaler can't add capacity, the tokenbucket throttle is still enforcing per-tenant limits. I'm seeing per-tier token refill set extremely low after a config roll earlier today. suspect combined effect: no new GPUs + aggressive token refill -> 429 cascade.

alice: can we temporary widen token refill or disable strict token enforcement for hotpath? we should aim to restore traffic for paying customers ASAP.

luke: we can patch policy to fallback to permissive tier for 10m. I'll craft a safe change: 
```
PATCH /config/ratepolicy/hotpath
{
  "tiers": [
    {"name":"prod-critical","refill_per_sec":2000,"burst":5000},
    {"name":"prod-default","refill_per_sec":1500,"burst":3000}
  ],
  "enforce_strict_tokens": false
}
```
Note: this allows higher bursts while we unstick autoscaler.

oncall-sre: good. raj, can you confirm we don't have billing/quotas blocking instance creation? need quick path to add nodes.

raj: quota on the cloud account is 0 for GPU SKUs due to a new org policy. I opened a support case but that's not going to be instant. Temporary workarounds: 1) move some low-priority workloads to CPU pools to free up GPUs, 2) activate burst-capacity license with partner pool (we have one in us-west-2), 3) manually migrate a small number of hotpath jobs to a compatible smaller model so they don't need GPUs.

silvia: I can start migrating low-priority jobs to CPU right now — making a filter for tag:background. Will post progress.

luke: while silvia migrates, I'm going to push the ratepolicy patch. rolling it to 10% of hotpath initially and watch.

oncall-sre: deploy the patch but keep the token window logging high verbosity. we need quick indicators: queued count, 429 rate, avg latency, and token refill rate per tier.

luke: PATCH rolled to 10% at 3117771200. monitoring: queued -> 5200 (was 6000), 429 -> 8% (was 12%), p50 latency unchanged.

maria: great signal. while this buys us breathing room, please throttle non-critical customers more aggressively in the edge router to preserve tokens for enterprise tiers. Add an explicit route rule: /v1/enterprise/* -> priority 100, /v1/free/* -> lower weight.

alice: applying edge rules now. small note: some customers use mixed endpoints; we'll add header-based priority override for those whitelisted accounts.

raj: silvia's migration freed two GPUs from background jobs. I just re-ran autoscaler provisioning; cloud provider accepted a 2-GPU allocation at 3117772400 (temporary burst pool). Autoscaler resumed and added nodes to hotpath.

incident-bot: NOTE: manual allocation added 2 GPUs to hotpath-prod at 3117772460 — monitoring required.

oncall-sre: with tokenpolicy relaxed and two GPUs live, queued dropped to 1800 within 10m. 429s down to 2.1% at 3117773300. Nice work.

amanda-sales: can we craft a short customer-facing update for the two impacted accounts? they asked for timeline.

alice: drafting now: "We experienced transient rate limiting due to capacity and config changes. We've applied a temporary mitigation, restored capacity, and are actively monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps." want this out in 20m?

maria: next steps for ops: 1) revert permissive tokenpolicy once autoscaler stable and GPUs >= baseline, 2) raise cloud GPU quota via support and schedule permanent partner-pool enablement, 3) add automated guardrail test to detect token refill regressions after config deploys.

luke: +1 on guardrail. I already have a PR that adds an e2e check that validates token refill != 0 after config apply. will fast-track it.

raj: I'll follow up on quota ticket and open a tracking RFC to make autoscaler fallback to partner pools automatically when quota denied.

oncall-sre: summary for post-incident: cause = cloud GPU quota policy + an overly restrictive tokenbucket config pushed earlier that amplified 429s; mitigation = relaxed ratepolicy, migrated background jobs, manual burst allocation -> autoscaler resumed; customer impact = transient 429s and increased latency for some customers, but core enterprise routes prioritized.

silvia: closing migration tasks. background jobs moved off GPUs at 3117774200.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: primary metrics returned to normal range at 3117774800. Please file a postmortem and include config diff and autoscaler logs.

oncall-sre: filing postmortem now. tagging eng-platform and eng-sre. Thanks everyone. :heart:
